title: Your Confidence Is Not Evidence
hook: Feeling confident is not proof you know it.
cta: Which topic are you most confidently wrong about?

slides.label: THE CONFIDENCE TRAP
slides.title: FEELING CONFIDENT
slides.body: A topic can feel familiar while your closed-book answer is still weak.
slides.callout: SWIPE TO CALIBRATE WHAT YOU KNOW →

slides.label: THE PROBLEM
slides.title: Your notes can
slides.body: While the explanation is visible, processing feels smooth. That feeling does not show what you can produce alone.

slides.label: STEP 01 — PREDICT
slides.title: Rate confidence
slides.body: Choose one question. Mark your confidence as low, medium, or high—then close the source.

slides.label: STEP 02 — RETRIEVE
slides.title: Answer from memory.
slides.body: Use clear criteria: key ideas, correct steps, and reasons. Do not grade the answer by how fluent it felt.

slides.label: STEP 03 — COMPARE
slides.title: Find the
slides.body: High confidence plus a weak answer is the blind spot to repair first. Correct but uncertain answers need reinforcement.

slides.label: THE NUANCE
slides.title: Confidence is useful
slides.body: One answer can be noisy. Compare confidence with results across several questions and look for a repeated pattern.
slides.callout: DO NOT TRUST A FEELING BY ITSELF

slides.label: THE CALIBRATION LOOP
slides.title: Predict. Retrieve.
slides.body: Repair confidently wrong answers first. Reinforce uncertain correct ones. Move on when strong performance repeats.
slides.callout: WHICH TOPIC ARE YOU MOST CONFIDENTLY WRONG ABOUT?
